question_type: two-cell difference across a series that was renamed, restructured and revised (vintage choice)
decisive_step: Whether the phrase 'using the reporting structure in which Air Force expenditures were still charged to Army appropriations' pins the ISSUE VINTAGE (the Aug-1947..Nov-1948 printings, FY1947 Army unrevised) or only identifies the COLUMN (the Army column that includes Air Force spending made from Army appropriations). Every later vintage footnotes the Army column the same way: 1948_08:324 (fn 10/), 1948_09:294-295 (fn 11/,12/), 1953_02:338-340 (fn 17/,18/) and the Feb-issue recap 'Table 6B - Detail of Expenditures by Months and Years' (1953_02:751 'Department of the Army 3/', fn 2/,3/ at 1953_02:1209-1211, which also says earlier years were 'reclassified and revised ... on a comparable basis'). So the phrase does not pin a date; the paper's convention (latest printing unless a date is pinned) then takes the FY1947 Army value revised in Dec 1948 (1948_12:224 'r', revision note 1948_12:326: 1947-appropriation items moved to 'International finance and aid', nothing to do with the Air Force) together with the FY1940 value that is identical in every printing (1948_08:227, 1953_02:754). The reference made the opposite choice at worklog Step 6 ('Chosen structure: the Jan-Aug 1948 ... tables ... Alternative rejected: [the Dec-1948 revision]') and was graded wrong; its rejected alternative sits ~7.6% below the submitted value, inside the 5-25pct error bin of every cell. The reference also claimed the later tables 'have no FY1940 Army value' (worklog Step 5), which Table 6B (1952_02:647, 1953_02:751) contradicts: one latest-vintage panel holds both FY1940 and the revised FY1947.

a.path_summary: find_tables on 'Air Force expenditures' (a[8]) surfaced the renamed Table 3 series; show_table 1948_08:225 (a[13]) gave the FY1940 Army cell (page cut before FY1947). printings on that title (a[15]) listed the FY1947 cell across 1948_03..1953 and a[16] explicitly noted that the latest printing is a revised, lower value. It then read the 1953_02 table and footnotes 17/18 (a[18], a[22]) — which say the Army column still 'includes certain expenditures on behalf of the Department of the Air Force' — but at a[23] decided the question phrase 'means' footnote 10 of the 1948_08 issue and subtracted the unrevised FY1947 value with calc (a[24]).

first_divergence.what_it_did: Read the question's column-definition phrase as a vintage pin ('use the pre-revision value because the revised structure excludes Air Force?'), guessed that the Dec-1948 revision was the Air Force split, and kept the unrevised FY1947 printing even after a[22] showed the latest footnotes keep Air Force spending inside the Army column.
first_divergence.what_a_right_cell_or_the_reference_did: No cell or the reference did it; the consistent path is: the phrase identifies the Army column (footnoted identically in every vintage), no issue is pinned, so take the latest printing of FY1947 Army (the 'r' value whose note at 1948_12:326 explains a reclassification to international aid) and the FY1940 value (same in all printings, also in Table 6B 1953_02:754).

smallest_change.change: printings: (1) follow a series across a title change and (2) print the revision note next to a revised value. Concretely, after the SUMMARY, when the title match covers fewer than 3 issues or when the same column label + row period exists in a later issue under another title in the same section, print: 'SERIES CONTINUES under another title: "Table 3. Expenditures for National Defense and Related Activities" (69 issues 1948_03..1954_03) prints FY1947 | "Department of the Army" too; latest printing 1953_02 (treasury_bulletin_1953_02.txt:232) = <value> r  - run printings --table "Expenditures for National Defense and Related Activities" --row FY1947 --col "Department of the Army"'. And for any cell carrying an r/revised flag, append the issue's revision footnote (the '*'/'r' note nearest below the table) as one line: '      revision note (1948_12:326): "Revised, in accordance with the Daily Treasury Statement of November 15, 1948, to include under International finance and aid expenditures from the 1947 appropriation which were formerly classified under military functions of the Department of the Army"'. Also keep the SUMMARY block ahead of the per-cell listing when the 8000-byte cap would cut it (a[15] lost the summary to 60 listing lines).
smallest_change.could_hurt_right_cells: unlikely - it adds lines; the only risk is a question that genuinely pins an early issue, and the line still names both values and issues so the text rule 'unless the question names a publication date or issue' still applies

alternatives.change: Add to the OfficeQA table notes: 'A phrase that says what a column includes or excludes (for example "Air Force expenditures still charged to Army appropriations") identifies the column, not the issue: it does not pin the vintage. Only a named publication date or issue does. Take the latest printing of that column and check, in the revision footnote, what the revision actually changed.'
alternatives.why_not_first: Cell a had 'latest printing unless the question names a publication date or issue' and still read the phrase as a pin at a[16]-a[23]; b and c never saw a later printing at all, so text alone leaves them blind.

alternatives.change: later_printing rule: look up the submitted cell by column label + row period across every table in the same section (not only the title-matched table id), so the renamed series is found; the finding would then have offered the revised FY1947 value in b[20].
alternatives.why_not_first: Only cell b has the gate; and the offer would arrive after the model already reasoned itself into the old vintage - the tool change shows the revision earlier, to all cells.

alternatives.change: find_tables: normalise OCR-damaged titles ('Expeditures' -> 'Expenditures') and show the panel subtitle ('Department of the Army 3/') for continuation parts of recap tables like Table 6B, whose columns are otherwise printed as bare '0..14' with the 'Fiscal year' label lost, so printings --col Army finds nothing in it.
alternatives.why_not_first: Table 6B is a second route to the same two values; the series-continuation line already exposes the revised FY1947 value.

fix.why_not_text: Cell a is the counter-example: it had the text, ran printings, saw at a[16] that the latest FY1947 printing is revised, and still chose the older vintage because it took the question's column-definition phrase as a date pin and guessed the revision was the Air Force split. What it lacked was the revision note (reclassification to international aid) and a clear statement that the later structure still includes Air Force spending in Army; both are tool outputs. Cells b and c never saw a later printing because the tool's title matching stopped at the renamed series, which no sentence can repair.
fix.irreducible: Partly. The wording 'using the reporting structure in which ...' invites the pre-revision reading; the strongest reference solver made the same choice with full reasoning and was graded wrong. The key's value is not visible here; the ~7.6%-low alternative (revised FY1947 minus FY1940) is inferred from the error bin and the paper's vintage convention, not verified.

notes: All three v9 cells, all three v8 arms and the reference converged on the same computation (older-vintage FY1947 minus FY1940), all in the 5-25pct bin, so this is a systematic convention miss, not model noise. Tool facts worth carrying into v10: (1) printings' series identity is an FTS phrase on the title, so a renamed table (Table 4 'Analysis of ...' -> Table 3 'Expenditures for ...' in 1948_03) splits one series into two and the old-title half reports 'same in all printings' with 1 printing - exactly the false reassurance b[16]/c[16] got; (2) the 1948_12 revision is flagged 'r' with its note at 1948_12:326, but printings never prints notes; (3) the Feb-issue recap 'Table 6B' (1952_02:647, 1953_02:751) is a single comparable-basis panel with both FY1940 and revised FY1947 for the Army, yet show_table renders its continuation part with header '0..14' (header borrowed) so the 'Fiscal year 1/' column is unlabeled and printings --col Army finds nothing; find_tables shows it as '[-]' with the OCR title 'Expeditures'; (4) show_table --grep is a substring, so a[11]'s regex alternation silently matched nothing; (5) b's later_printing control inherits the tool's blind spot and did not fire.
